query: For rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys intended for magnetic refrigeration, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs a strong magnetocaloric response at low applied fields while maintaining rapid heat exchange, low hysteresis, and mechanical stability? State one controlled intervention that would test the hypothesis, the observations predicted relative to a baseline, the boundaries over which the hypothesis should hold, prior evidence that would support it, and an outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Enhancing local chemical short-range order (SRO) in a Fe–Mn–Cr–Co–Ni high-entropy alloy tunes magnetic exchange and magnetoelastic coupling to produce a sharp, low-hysteresis magnetostructural transition, yielding a large magnetocaloric entropy change at low applied fields while preserving rapid heat exchange and mechanical integrity.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic Fe–Mn–Cr–Co–Ni HEA produced by arc melting and rapid quenching to a fully disordered fcc solid solution.
generation.intervention: Heat treat the as-quenched alloy at 650 °C for 48 h to promote Fe–Cr and Mn–Ni pairwise SRO without inducing second-phase precipitation.
generation.conditions: Magnetic characterization from 100 K to 300 K under fields up to 0.5 T; thermal cycling at 1 K/min; mechanical load up to 200 MPa.
generation.structural_mediator: Degree of local chemical SRO, quantified by diffuse scattering intensity ratio (ordered/disordered) in X-ray or neutron diffraction.
generation.mechanism: Increased SRO sharpens the magnetostructural transformation by homogenizing local exchange interactions and enhancing magnetoelastic coupling, increasing ΔS_M at low fields and narrowing transformation hysteresis, while more uniform microstructure maintains thermal conductivity and mechanical stability.
generation.predicted_outcome: Annealed (SRO-enhanced) samples show ≥20% higher peak isothermal entropy change ΔS_M at 0.5 T, ≥30% narrower thermal hysteresis, and ≥10% higher thermal conductivity versus the disordered baseline, with no loss in compressive yield strength.
generation.baseline: As-quenched, fully disordered HEA: ΔS_M≈1 J·kg⁻¹·K⁻¹ at 0.1 T, hysteresis width ≈4 K, thermal conductivity ≈10 W·m⁻¹·K⁻¹, compressive yield strength ≈600 MPa.
generation.boundary: Holds for compositions within ±5 at% of equiatomic Fe–Mn–Cr–Co–Ni, annealing temperatures 600–700 °C for 24–72 h, and applied fields 0.1–1 T.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate; long anneals may nucleate unwanted intermetallics that disrupt SRO–magnetism link.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare three sample sets: (a) as-quenched, (b) annealed at 650 °C for 24 h, (c) annealed at 650 °C for 48 h. Measure SRO via diffraction, magnetization vs temperature at 0.5 T, compute ΔS_M, record thermal hysteresis width, measure thermal conductivity, and perform compressive stress tests.
measurements: isothermal magnetic entropy change (ΔS_M) at 0.5 T
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If samples with increased SRO (by >20% in diffraction intensity ratio) do not exhibit at least a 10% increase in ΔS_M or a 10% reduction in hysteresis compared to as-quenched, the hypothesis is falsified.
